 Preview: Stanford Men’s Basketball welcomes Oakland to Maples Pavilion
 Ben Parker @ slamdunk406 7h 0 Share Share 
 Nov 2, 2026; Stanford, California, USA; Stanford Cardinal guard Julius Price (5) drives past a Eastern Washington Eagles forward Jamil Miller as Stanford Cardinal forward Nick Townsend (42) sets a screen during the first half at Maples Pavilion. Mandatory Credit: D. Ross Cameron-Imagn Images 
 On Friday at 7:00 PM PT on ACCNX, Stanford men’s basketball will welcome the Oakland Golden Grizzlies to Maples Pavilion. The Grizzlies hail from the state of Michigan. Not the East Bay. Stanford comes in at 1-0 overall while Oakland comes in at 0-1.
 Last time out: Stanford defeated Eastern Washington 74-65 on Monday. Stanford freshman point guard Julius Price led the way for the Cardinal with 17 points and four assists.
 RECAP: Stanford Men’s Basketball wins season opener against Eastern Washington 
 On Oakland: The Grizzlies dropped their first game of the season on the road at No. 16 Michigan on Monday, losing 84-68, battling the Wolverines tough. Three guys scored in double figures for the Grizzlies in that game: Forward Chris Fields Jr. (18 points & 10 rebounds), guard Nassim Mashhour (16 points & 4 rebounds), and guard Ryder Bradley (12 points & 4 steals).
 Head coach Greg Kampe has been at the helm since the 1984-85 season, guiding them from the Division II level to the Division I level, starting in 1999-2000. He’s got a lot of experience and knows what he’s doing. His teams often have good perimeter shooters and also play a lot of zone defense. Last season, they went 16-16 overall and 12-8 in the Horizon League, good for third place.
 Keys to the game: For Stanford, the first thing they need to do is not get off to an icy cold shooting start. They got down double digits early against Eastern Washington due to poor shooting from the perimeter. Given the Grizzlies play a zone, if they attack it right, that could lead to some good 3-point opportunities. Stanford just has to make sure they knock them down.
 Secondly, Stanford needs to make sure they contain Fields and Mashhour. Both guys were a bit shy of scoring in double figures last season on average, Fields also is a transfer from Campbell. That said, they both really balled out against Michigan. If Stanford can defend those two guys well, they should be in good shape to win this game.
 Third, Stanford needs to keep applying good pressure defensively. Aziz Olajwuon with six steals was excellent on Monday. If they can keep up that kind of defensive pressure, they should be in good shape.
 Finally, Stanford needs to make sure they win the battle on the glass. Rebounding is a big point of emphasis that head coach Kyle Smith has been making leading up to the season. This is a game where Stanford hopefully controls the glass and wins on that front.
 Prediction: I got Stanford winning this game, though given how tough Oakland played Michigan, I think it’ll be a competitive game. Stanford 77 Oakland 67 is how I see this one going.
